summary.text: Son of Evanthes, priest of Apollo, who dwelt at Ismarus in the land of the Cicones — he gave Odysseus dark sweet wine in twelve jars, unmixed and divine, together with gold and a silver bowl, and his wife added cloaks and mantles; that wine later blinded Polyphemus.

story.text: When Odysseus sacked Ismarus, city of the Cicones, Maron son of Evanthes received him kindly because he revered the god. He gave twelve jars of sweet wine, a drink unmixed and divine — one cup of it poured into twenty of water still bore a sweet smell — and seven talents of gold and a silver mixing-bowl; his wife, daughter of Maron, gave twelve cloaks and as many mantles.
Odysseus carried that vintage aboard the ships; in the Cyclops' cave he gave Polyphemus the Maronean wine to drink, and when the giant slept drunk the Greeks drove the heated stake into his one eye.
He must not be confused with Maron the Lacedaemonian honoured at Sparta beside Alpheius after Thermopylae — a different man who shares only the name.
